To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the autocorrelations of transverse-momenta fluctuations in Hijing simulations of Au–Au collisions are dominated by a same-sided azimuthal peak with similar widths in pseudorapidity and azimuth, and that this peak becomes broader and weaker when jet quenching is imposed.

the scale dependence of the 〈 p t 〉 fluctuation is well represented by a Gaussian distribution with a standard deviation that is approximately constant with centrality and is approximately 0.2 in the range 0.2 < p t < 3 GeV / c, and that the autocorrelation distribution is dominated by a same-sided (on azimuth) minijet peak, which is slightly broadened by jet quenching.
Hijing-simulations of Au–Au collisions with and without jet quenching predict a similar structure for the autocorrelations of event-wise transverse momentum fluctuations.

The main takeaway from our work is that
the scale dependence of event-wise 〈 p t 〉 is a sensitive probe of minijets in heavy-ion collisions.
the same-side peaks are a robust feature of the event-wise 〈 p t 〉 distributions, and are not affected by the choice of bin-size or by the imposition of jet quenching.
the same-side peak is a robust feature of minijets, and it is a promising signature to identify and quantify minijets in experimental data.
